avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 inducer; increases loratadine metabolism and reduces plasma concentrations
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use or monitor for reduced antihistamine efficacy; consider alternative herbal supplement

avoid_supplements.name: Ketoconazole (oral)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibitor; significantly increases loratadine metabolite exposure and QT interval risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid combination; use alternative antifungal if necessary

caution_supplements.name: Grapefruit seed extract
caution_supplements.mechanism: Weak CYP3A4 inhibition may slightly increase loratadine levels
caution_supplements.action: Limit intake or monitor for increased drowsiness or dry mouth

caution_supplements.name: Quercetin
caution_supplements.mechanism: Natural antihistamine with additive effects; may enhance sedation risk
caution_supplements.action: Use together cautiously and counsel patient on possible increased drowsiness

caution_foods.name: Grapefruit juice
caution_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition increases loratadine active metabolite concentrations
caution_foods.action: Limit grapefruit juice consumption or separate dosing by several hours

caution_foods.name: Alcohol
caution_foods.mechanism: Additive CNS depression; loratadine is non-sedating but alcohol may potentiate any residual effects
caution_foods.action: Advise patient to limit or avoid alcohol; counsel on potential impaired cognitive/motor function

monitoring_notes: Loratadine has minimal interaction potential due to low systemic bioavailability and CYP3A4/2D6 metabolism; most interactions affect active metabolite desloratadine rather than parent drug. Monitor for loss of efficacy with CYP3A4 inducers and increased adverse effects with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors.
